highlights: HNB Stockbrokers keeps Sampath Bank at Buy with a 12-month target of Rs 190 (23% upside from Rs 154; 0.9x P/BV), well above this site's fair value of Rs 144 (buy below Rs 122): the broker is about 32% more optimistic.

Sampath's September quarter: loans +3.3% q/q to Rs 1,591bn, NIM steady at 4.22%, but forex and trading losses of Rs 4.7bn and higher impairment cut profit 21.3% q/q to Rs 8.7bn; NPL ratio improved to 1.9%.

A weak day on 13 Nov: banks fell (HNB −1.88%, Sampath −1.91%, NDB and NTB −1.29%, DFCC −2.80%) with Commercial Bank flat, and John Keells slipped 1.52%; Dialog (+0.40%) and Ceylon Tobacco (+1.05%) held up.

Dipped Products' September quarter: revenue Rs 25.3bn (+19.5% year on year) and EPS Rs 2.53 (+64.4%), its best quarter in two years; P/E 9.5x and P/B 1.15x at Rs 71.10. The shares rose 3.94% on 13 Nov.
Ceylon Tobacco declared a third interim dividend of Rs 41.00 (XD 23 Nov, paid 11 Dec); the broker puts the trailing dividend yield at 8.9% at Rs 1,809.50.
2027 Budget: tax relief for the middle class and record capital spending; the President said public debt should fall to 87% of GDP by 2032, better than the earlier 95% target.

news.title: Sampath Bank: Q3 2026 earnings note (HNB Stockbrokers)
news.text: Gross loans grew 3.3% q/q to Rs 1,591bn and deposits 5.2% to Rs 1,874bn; CASA eased to 33.7%. Interest income rose 7.3% but interest expense 11.0%, leaving NIM at 4.22% (4.21% in Q2). Fee income rose 8.1%, but forex and trading losses of Rs 4.7bn (a Rs 4.0bn profit in Q2) cut total operating income 15.5% to Rs 31.6bn. Costs rose 5.8%, lifting cost-to-income to 49.7%; impairment rose 146.8% from a low Q2 base. The effective tax rate fell to 41.1% and profit to shareholders fell 21.3% q/q to Rs 8.7bn. NPL ratio 1.9% (2.3% in Q2) with 68.7% cover; Tier 1 12.3%, total capital 15.3%. Rating Buy, target Rs 190 (0.9x P/BV), short-term outlook Neutral; 52-week range Rs 136–164, market cap Rs 180.6bn. Risks: deposit repricing and the new Tier 2 issue could squeeze margins. Catalysts: loan-to-deposit ratio of 84.9% leaves room to lend more; the new wealth management business. Peer table (as of 12 Nov): SAMP P/E 5.0x, P/BV 0.9x, ROE 18.6%, dividend yield 6.7%; HNB 5.0x, 0.7x, 15.2%, 3.7%; COMB 5.8x, 1.0x, 19.0%, 3.6%; NTB 4.4x, 1.0x, 24.2%, 1.1%.

news.title: Dipped Products: Q2 2026/27 results
news.text: Revenue Rs 25,338mn against Rs 21,196mn a year earlier (+19.5%), up 1.25% on the June quarter. EPS Rs 2.53 against Rs 1.54 (+64.4%), up from Rs 2.06 in the June quarter. The broker's card shows a trailing P/E of 9.53x and P/B of 1.15x at the 12 Nov close of Rs 71.10.

news.text: The President, also finance minister, presented the government's third budget: middle-class tax relief, record capital spending, and a forecast that public debt falls to 87% of GDP by 2032 (earlier target 95%).

news.text: Private-sector credit reached Rs 2.1tn in the first nine months of 2026, with short-term loans taking a larger share; lawmakers asked whether enough is going into new investment and capacity.

news.text: Sri Lanka is seeking a new free trade agreement with China, and officials reviewed progress towards the US$5bn ICT/BPM export target for 2030.
